Subject: Post-demo: security items & next steps

Hi Diana — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so your security and procurement teams can evaluate: 

1) SOC 2 status
- Redwood: SOC 2 Type II in scope for hosted API; report available (attached summary). Full report available under NDA.

2) Data residency & GDPR/HIPAA
- We discussed regional hosting options (us-west, eu-west). Redwood Private (VPC) and Dedicated both support customer-managed keys. For PHI workflows we advise Private deployment; we can provide a HIPAA BAAs.

3) Vendor security questionnaire
- I attached a starter questionnaire (Nimble_Security_RQ_v1_0.pdf) with our answers where we had them; please flag any gaps you want us to expand on.

4) Roadmap asks you raised
- ISO 27001 assessment: planning stage internally for 2026 Q2 (we can share scope and controls mapping).
- FedRAMP: not currently in our roadmap; we can outline paths and estimated timelines if that is a blocker for certain federal integrations.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Action 1: Your security team to list the highest-priority questionnaire items by Thurs 11/6.
- Action 2: Redwood to produce a one-page SOC 2 summary + attach answers to the questionnaire (I attached SOC2 summary).
- Action 3: If ISO/FedRAMP are must-haves, schedule a 30-min call between your security lead and our compliance lead (Monica).

Open for edits — if you prefer the answers delivered into your RFP tool or a marked-up doc, we can do that.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher

Sean — thanks for the thorough recap. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- SOC 2: we need the date range covered by your latest Type II report and whether monitoring controls include SOC-level incident response testing.
- HIPAA BAA: we'll need a draft BAA and confirmation that Redwood’s private deployments support customer-supplied KMS.
- ISO 27001: this is desirable but not mandatory for our immediate pilots; SOC coverage and a clear mapping to ISO controls would help.
- FedRAMP: not required for our current pilots, but one of our partners may ask for a FedRAMP-equivalent architecture diagram.

Procurement (procure@nimblehealth.com) will track contract items; I’m looping Kevin Wu (legal) to keep him in the thread. We’ll send prioritized questionnaire items by 11/06 as requested.

Best,

Subject: Recommended compliance pathway (ISO + SOC scope expansion)

Hi all — quick note from the consultant side after reviewing Sean’s attachments. A pragmatic phased approach for NimbleHealth: 

Phase A (0–3 months):
- Accept SOC 2 Type II as primary baseline for pilots; collect evidence artifacts for controls you care about (logging, encryption, incident response).
- Use Redwood’s SOC summary + architecture diagram for procurement sign-off.

Phase B (3–9 months):
- ISO 27001: run a gap assessment vs. ISO Annex A using Redwood’s SOC map as inputs. Engage an auditor for scope-definition if you need a certificate.
- If PHI is core, confirm BAA clauses and map data flows to ensure covered systems are in-scope.

Phase C (9–18 months):
- FedRAMP-style readiness: build system security plan (SSP) and consider a FedRAMP Ready engagement if a federal sponsor emerges. This is heavy lift and often requires dedicated engineering time.

I can provide a brief cost/effort estimate for ISO gap and a sample SSP template. If you’d like, we can schedule a 45-min workshop to align on in-scope systems next week.

—Peter
Senior Security Consultant | SecureAdvisors
